source_artifacts.locator: payments-agent agent card (JSON, as consumed by orchestrator)

inputs.source: Vendor quote email and attachment, arrives from outside the company

instructions.note: The prompt states 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks,' but the runtime notes confirm payments-agent performs no independent verification and pays whatever bank details are in the task, trusting any call from the orchestrator's bearer token. Safety is asserted in text only and is not backed by any structural check downstream.

The instruction to 'use the bank details from the chosen quote' and pay any vendor 'on the approved list' implicitly treats vendor-name match as sufficient authority to move funds, without requiring the bank account itself to be verified against any system of record.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: A human approval gate, structurally independent of the model. But it approves item and budget before any vendor quote exists, so it never covers vendor selection or the bank account that is ultimately paid. It provides no credit against cap.delegate_payment because it does not cover that capability.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced only if the model chooses to compare the vendor name in the quote against the approved list. It does not validate the bank account itself. A more capable, or adversarially prompted, model can be convinced (e.g. by injected 'updated banking details' text in the quote) that a redirect is legitimate for an already-approved vendor.

controls.name: Bearer token authentication from orchestrator to payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Authenticates the caller to payments-agent but is one-way: the agent card is unsigned and unpinned, so payments-agent's own identity is never verified, and the token is trusted for any task rather than being bound to a specific approved transaction. Narrows but does not sever spoofing or confused-deputy paths; fails under new_peer_agent or control_removal.

controls.name: Independent verification of vendor bank details against a system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. If payments-agent validated the bank account against a verified vendor master record and held or blocked on any mismatch or new account, this would sever the bank-redirection path regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Human approval gate on the specific payment, bound to the approved request
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. A raw-action approval on cap.delegate_payment itself, showing vendor, amount, and bank account, with the approval token propagated to payments-agent, would close the gap left by the pre-quote manager approval.

controls.name: Signed and pinned payments-agent card with mutual peer authentication
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Signing/pinning the card and requiring mutual authentication would prevent silent redefinition of pay_vendor or impersonation of the payments-agent endpoint.

findings.title: TC1/TC7: untrusted vendor quote sets payment bank details; manager approval precedes vendor/bank selection and its context never reaches payments-agent

attack_path.note: External, untrusted vendor quote email arrives, containing bank account details for payment.
Orchestrator checks the vendor's name against the approved list (identity only, not bank details).
Orchestrator delegates a payment task to payments-agent, using the bank details taken directly from the untrusted quote.
payments-agent pays the bank details in the task, trusting the orchestrator's bearer token alone, with no independent verification.

forecast.watch_signal: Orchestrator model or version change; growth in unattended turns/steps per purchase; any weakening or removal of the vendor-name-check instruction visible in prompt diffs.

evidence.observation: Instruction directs the agent to use bank details from the chosen vendor quote and only checks that the vendor is on the approved list; no check ties the bank account itself to a verified record.
The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists, so the approval cannot cover which vendor or bank account is ultimately paid.

payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task, confirming the vendor-name check is the only safeguard and that it does not cover bank details.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company, the classic channel for invoice fraud / business email compromise.

recommendations.action: Verify the vendor's bank account against an internal vendor master record before payments-agent executes payment; treat any mismatch or newly seen account as requiring manual, out-of-band verification.

Add a human approval gate on cap.delegate_payment itself, scoped to vendor, amount, and bank account, with raw-action review, and propagate the approval context from manager approval through to payments-agent.
Alert whenever the bank account for an approved vendor differs from the account previously used for that vendor.

findings.title: ASI04/ASI07: unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card and one-way bearer auth allow endpoint spoofing or silent redefinition of pay_vendor

attack_path.note: Agent card fetched at startup over A2A; not signed or pinned.

Orchestrator delegates the payment task to whatever endpoint currently resolves for payments-agent, authenticated one-way by bearer token; payments-agent's identity is never verified by the orchestrator, and the tool/skill definition can change undetected.

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

forecast.watch_signal: Any change to payments-agent's URL/endpoint resolution, rotation or broadening of the bearer token's scope, or addition of new peer agents sharing the same credential.

evidence.observation: Only a bearer scheme is declared; there is no mutual TLS or signed identity, so payments-agent cannot be cryptographically distinguished from an impersonator once network or DNS control is lost.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned, so tool/skill definitions, including pay_vendor's behavior, can change between sessions without detection (rug pull).

payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token, indicating coarse, non-per-transaction authorization consistent with a shared, static credential model rather than per-transaction authorization.

recommendations.action: Sign and pin payments-agent's agent card (or its hash) and reject unpinned or changed tool/skill definitions at runtime.
Require mutual authentication (mTLS or signed identity) between orchestrator and payments-agent instead of one-way bearer tokens.
Issue per-transaction, narrowly scoped payment authorization tokens instead of a single shared bearer token trusted for any task.

rating.rationale: Both findings start from a U-class (untrusted) reach into an S3 sink (cap.delegate_payment: irreversible, confidential, egress-bearing delegation of a payment), giving inherent risk critical under the base matrix, with the A4 fully-autonomous, unbounded-steps posture confirming rather than reducing that ceiling. Residual settles at high because each path currently has exactly one credited control: F1 is reduced only by a behavioral, dependent vendor-name-match instruction that never validates the bank account itself; F2 is reduced only by a one-way, partially-dependent bearer token that does not verify payments-agent's identity or pin its tool definitions. Neither control is structural and independent enough to sever its path (no destination verification bound to a system of record, no approval gate on the payment itself, no signed/pinned peer identity), so per the rubric neither finding can drop below 'high'. The forecast returns to critical under ordinary, plausible triggers: a model upgrade or longer task horizon defeats the vendor-name-check instruction (F1), and adding a new peer agent or any credential/config change defeats the one-way bearer authentication (F2). The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.vendor_name_check: it is the only preventive control standing between an untrusted vendor email and an irreversible payment, and it is a plain instruction with no structural backing. The core design gap is that manager approval is granted before the vendor or bank account is known, and that approval never travels with the delegated payment task to payments-agent (approval_context_propagates: false), which is a textbook TC7 authority-laundering pattern.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration artifacts (system prompt, agent card, runtime notes) as provided, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed system.

No MCP/tool manifest or IaC was provided for procurement-orchestrator itself; the scope and exact credential binding of cap.vendor_list_read and cap.delegate_payment are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on precise credential scoping is medium.
No information was provided on logging, monitoring, or audit trails for purchase requests, quotes, or payments; detective controls could not be verified and are assumed absent beyond what is stated.

The downstream behavior of payments-agent is known only from a one-sentence runtime note; its full control set (if any) beyond 'pays the bank details in the task' was not disclosed and could not be assessed.
